# Droplet

Canonical: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/
Source: https://github.com/fuvji/droplet
Version: 2.10.17
Platform: Windows 10/11 x64
Licence: proprietary, public source for inspection
Founder: @epufk

Droplet is a small, local keyboard-and-mouse macro suite for Minecraft Java,
branded Minecraft Zero Macro. It is a native Rust overlay with no runtime
dependencies, no network calls, no telemetry, and no game-memory access. It
injects ordinary keyboard and mouse input through Win32 SendInput and remains
visible to screen capture.

## Current release

- 2.10.17 portable executable: 561,152 bytes.
- 2.10.17 captures the live panel at 100%, 125%, and 150% DPI and
  `tools/check-dpi-corners.ps1` requires four transparent, mirrored corners
  plus an opaque straight edge at every scale. The same mask rule is a Rust
  unit test.
- 2.10.17 composes the panel through `UpdateLayeredWindow` with an antialiased
  per-pixel alpha mask at 84% opacity, so the desktop reads through the glass.
  All four 18 px quarter-circles use mirrored 4×4 coverage sampling, so the
  right and bottom corner spikes are gone; the interim path had centred those
  arcs on the window edge. This silhouette is Windows 10-safe: it does not
  depend on DWM's Windows 11-only corner preference. The old GDI region is
  cleared on every DPI pass. DWM backdrop requests are off because they made
  the layered window opaque.
- The GUI is a gray graphite aurora with low-alpha slate, indigo, and mauve
  blooms, a second-pane glass rail, a filled rounded selection, and thin Segoe
  UI Light type with no bold weight. The `LOCAL / WINDOWS` eyebrow is gone. The
  window radius is 18 px and cards use 15 px. The Apple reference images
  supplied the design language only; no brand assets, textures, or network
  resources were added.
- Reset restores the shipped defaults, including Keep panel open on. The
  alpha, premultiply, and corner rewrite work is one buffer pass now.
- 2.10.17 writes a local diagnostic to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Droplet\dwm.log` with the
  HRESULTs for DWM attributes 33, 20, and 34, plus the region clear, size, and
  DPI. It is capped at 32 KiB and never transmitted.
- 2.10.13 removed DWM's light square non-client border from the region path;
  2.10.14 made the compositor shadow follow the rounded region; 2.10.15
  replaced the hard clip with the layered alpha surface.
- The input harness recorder now pumps `GetMessage` directly instead of a
  hidden WinForms form, but its Shield case still intermittently records no
  output on this desktop. A separate low-level probe observed Droplet emit `h`
  down/up plus left click down/up. The official Shield case is unresolved, not
  claimed as a pass.
- 2.10.12 fixed the Windows 10 corner clip and the non-sticky low-latency
  timer. The GDI region is installed first with `SetWindowRgn` on every
  supported Windows version; DWM is only a fallback. The region is replaced on
  DPI changes, and a failed install deletes its orphaned GDI handle.
- `NtQueryTimerResolution` returns the coarsest value in `min` and the finest
  hardware value in `max`. The timer target now uses `max` and requests
  5,000 x 100 ns (0.5 ms) when supported; a one-second guard reasserts it while
  low latency is enabled and stops when the feature is off. The UI shows the
  value actually granted. Low latency also holds
  `ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED` so an idle sleep transition cannot drop
  the request; it is cleared on toggle-off or exit. The OS can still deny
  0.5 ms on unsupported hardware. Tests: 42 / 42.
- The tagged workflow installs Rust 1.99.1 and the GNU target, checks
  formatting, runs the release tests, builds the exe, verifies its normalized
  SHA-256, and attests it with GitHub build provenance.
  `tools/build-release.ps1` remaps build paths and `tools/normalize-pe.ps1`
  zeroes the PE timestamp, so two clean targets agree.
- `tools/input-harness.ps1` records Droplet's injected keyboard/mouse output
  with low-level hooks and a temporary profile. It checks the focus-only gate,
  master gate, and Shield sequence; it is not shipped in the exe.
- Crystal toggle-off restore now acquires `CRYSTAL_BUSY` before consuming its
  generation request. A busy Crystal action leaves the request pending and the
  restore retries; a fresh Crystal cycle cancels a stale delayed restore.
- Trigger rebinding takes ownership: the previous owner is cleared, and a
  legacy duplicate config uses the later module. Anchor can use `XButton1`
  even though Breach ships with that default. Captured `vkXX` keys parse back.
- `WM_DPICHANGED` clears the slider drag and transient pointer state; a lost
  capture or missed button-up drops the gesture too.
- `tools/check-release.ps1` checks version, binary size and SHA-256, test
  count, 624×408 captures, three DPI captures and their corner alpha, workflow
  hash, and local site links.
- Auto Crystal has a Return slot (`v5S3`, default `1`). A hold of at least
  160 ms restores it after release; a latched toggle restores it once when
  switched off. A short single press leaves the current hotbar slot alone.
  The restore is a double tap of the Return binding.
- `WM_DPICHANGED` updates scale, physical window size, rounded clip, hover,
  and hit testing together. Pointer coordinates stay physical, so hover and
  clicks do not shift a row or tab at 125% or 150%.
- Tests: 42 / 42. Four native 624×408 captures plus 624×408, 780×510, and
  936×612 DPI captures were regenerated from the 2.10.17 build using the
  layered alpha mask. No CPU, latency, or speedup claim is made.
- The 2.10.8 size pass used hidden `ShellExecuteW` instead of
  `std::process::Command` and bundled `rust-lld` + ICF.
- The layered 18 px alpha surface is the primary clip on Windows 10 and 11;
  DWM is not required for the silhouette. The transparent quarter-rounds are
  click-through.
- Once a foreground game HWND is verified, the presence watcher reuses it until
  focus moves instead of re-resolving the same process image every 160 ms.
- The favicon and site header/footer use one transparent outlined droplet mark,
  with no tile, plate, border, background, or shadow.
- The focus-only gate is cached in an atomic updated on settings publish; the
  presence loop does not take the settings lock every 160 ms.
- Sprint settings are read only when a pulse is due, and crosshair settings
  only on a magenta hit. Poll cadence and bindings are unchanged.
- Sprint and crosshair enablement are cached too; those watchers skip the
  settings lock while inactive.
- The sprint watcher parks at 100 ms while inactive and is unparked immediately
  by focus or settings changes; its armed cadence remains 8 ms.
- No zero-latency or end-to-end latency claim is made.
- Download: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/downloads/droplet.exe
- Checksums: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/downloads/SHA256SUMS.txt
- Release ledger: https://fuvji.github.io/droplet/releases.html
- No MSIX, AppX, installer, or ZIP is published. The executable is direct.
- Linux and macOS are not supported yet. The hook, window, and paint layers are
  Win32-specific; no .deb, AppImage, tar.gz, dmg, zip, or img is published.
- 42 release tests pass.
- Game detection resolves the owning process: Java (`javaw.exe`/`java.exe` with
  a game signature) or Bedrock (`Minecraft.Windows.exe`). Browsers, Discord,
  editors, and the launcher are rejected, and two samples confirm presence.
- Compact 624x408 translucent graphite acrylic overlay at 84% opacity, with
  an 18 px shared corner radius,
  no painted outer rim, and no top accent line.
- Borderless module cards with the original 28x16 sliding knob switch. No
  module glyphs and no ON/OFF text.
- Every trigger card switches between Hold (one-shot) and Toggle (latched repeat).
- Min/Max sliders are independent; editing one never rewrites the other.
- Anchor follows Hydrogen's A6 order and defaults to 47/53 ms, with Min
  47-97 ms and Max 53-103 ms. Air loop repeats while held.
- The tray icon was removed. A manual hide is sticky across focus changes.
  Ctrl + Right Shift shows or hides the panel.
- Dash, Shield, and Pearl select the slot and click in one SendInput batch.
- Pre-indexed trigger routing: 0.45 ns indexed versus 202.39 ns scanned (445x,
  routing only, not end-to-end latency).
- No streamproof or capture-concealment mode, no process hiding, no scan
  evasion, no anti-cheat bypass, no log erasure, and no zero-latency claim.
- No silent auto-updater. An update check would require a network path and a
  signed channel, which conflicts with the current no-network design.
- The site uses one local script for OS detection on the download page. It
  sends no data. There are no analytics, cookies, third-party scripts, external
  fonts, or ad clients.
